Jamie: Quick follow-up on the offload allocator RFC — I prototyped a 'reservoir backpressure' flow to avoid eviction storms when host-staging saturates. Posting experiment notes.
Vikram: Nice. TL;DR what does 'reservoir' mean here?
Jamie: Essentially a soft quota per-tenant on staging pages + token-bucket style admit. When queue empty it drains. When over threshold we stop admitting new stage requests and return fast-fail or route to cached variants.
Maria: Could you paste the admission pseudo-config?
Jamie: Sure:
```
offload:
  reservoir:
    capacity_pages: 512
    burst_pages: 64
    refill_rate_per_s: 32
    backpressure_action: retry-500 | route-fallback
```
This is the test YAML used in bench runs.
Sasha: How do you prevent global imbalance — one tenant hogging reservoir across GPUs?
Jamie: We shard per-GPU+tenant token buckets. There's also a global reclaim hook: if overall host usage < 70% we push tokens back to hungry tenants. Added lease timeouts to avoid leaks.
Evan: What about fairness when batching interacts? Say a big batch pins many pages then drains tokens.
Jamie: Good point. Current heuristic charges the reservoir proportional to active request size; we also have a batch-window cap so no single request can consume > X% of its tenant's burst.
Vikram: Any perf numbers?
Jamie: Micro-bench on small 1k token seqs: ~30% fewer OOM-driven evictions, p99 latency regressed ~3ms due to extra checks. End-to-end throughput improved under noisy neighbors.
Maria: Ops implications? Rollout plan?
Jamie: Start in canary region with `reservoir.enabled=true|false` flag, collect metrics: `reservoir_admits`, `reservoir_denies`, `reservoir_reclaims`, and `staging_evictions`. If denies > 0.5% for a tenant we add a canary alert.
ops-bot: deploy plan generated: canary -> 5% -> 25% -> global; pause if `reservoir_denies` spike.
Sasha: Failure modes? What if the refill daemon crashes?
Jamie: Tokens persist in local disk checkpoint every 10s; on restart we rehydrate. Worst-case we default to permissive (no backpressure) for 30s then ramp up conservative refill to avoid immediate storms.
Evan: I worry about complexity in allocator ABI. Does this require new APIs for `stage_request(size)` returning admit/deny?
Jamie: Yes small API change: `stage_request(size, tenant_id) -> {admit, token_cost, lease_id}` and `stage_release(lease_id)`; fallback path remains unchanged. We tried to keep it additive.
Vikram: OK. Can we get a short RFC PR with the API surface, config, and rollout metrics? I'll review.
Jamie: Will open PR today. Also attaching quick synthetic log snippet to validate we get denies when we expect:
```
[2026-03-19T14:12:03Z] tenant=acme admits=1 cost=12
[2026-03-19T14:12:04Z] tenant=acme denies=1 reason=reservoir_cap
[2026-03-19T14:12:05Z] tenant=acme reclaim=8 reclaimed_from=tenant-42
```
Maria: Sounds good. +1 to canary-first. :thumbsup:
Jamie: Thanks — will send PR link and benchmark graphs shortly.
